stories.headline: Government completes final budget framework review amid austerity, S&P downgrades outlook
stories.summary: The Orpo-Purra government concluded its final kehysriihi (budget framework negotiation) on April 21-22 at Säätytalö, setting fiscal guidelines for 2027-2030 with approximately €520 million in supplementary savings, increases to healthcare fees, expanded home renovation tax credits, a peat energy support package, and reversal of Marin-era YEL self-employment pension reform. Standard & Poor's immediately downgraded Finland's credit outlook to negative, warning Helsinki has no time to wait until the next parliamentary elections to address debt trajectory.

stories.headline: Opposition demands PM Orpo resign over fiscal failure; Orpo refuses at Yle interview, SDP prepares interpellation
stories.summary: Following the kehysriihi, SDP leader Antti Lindtman and Greens leader Sofia Virta publicly demanded PM Orpo's resignation, citing failure on all fiscal and employment targets. Orpo rejected the calls in a live Yle Radio Finland prime ministerial interview on April 26, defending the government's record. SDP simultaneously announced it would table an interpellation on economic and employment policy and published a new 72-page political programme, while polls showed Kokoomus support at a five-year low.

stories.headline: Finnish Defence Forces calls up reserve volunteers for readiness exercises following drone incidents
stories.summary: The Finnish Defence Forces announced it was activating consent-based reserve soldiers (suostumusreserviläiset) for refresher exercises across the country, explicitly linked to drone incidents over Finnish territory earlier in spring and broader situational awareness needs. The exercises were conducted with unusual operational secrecy — locations, participant numbers, and duration were not disclosed. Defence Minister Häkkänen confirmed the kehysriihi allocated over €1.39 billion in additional defence procurement authorisations.

stories.headline: US halts weapons deliveries to Baltic states; Finland says its defence capability unaffected
stories.summary: US-supplied HIMARS and Javelin deliveries to Baltic states were reported paused, according to Estonian and regional media; Estonia's defence minister confirmed the suspension. Finnish political leadership commented that any potential halt would not affect Finland's defence capacity, with PM Orpo stating he believed the issue was production-related rather than political. Defence Minister Häkkänen declined to comment on specific deliveries but called for accelerated European defence industry capacity.

stories.headline: Orpo attends EU Cyprus informal summit; backs Ukraine loan package and Russia sanctions, cautious on EU membership timeline
stories.summary: PM Orpo attended the EU informal European Council in Nicosia and Ayia Napa on April 23-24, praising agreement on a Ukraine loan package and new Russia sanctions. Orpo stated that setting a specific year target for Ukraine's EU membership was unrealistic, though Finland supports accession on a merit-based schedule. He also noted that Hungary's election result (Orbán defeat) opened possibilities for less obstructed Ukraine membership discussions.

stories.headline: EU/NATO mutual defence debate intensifies at Cyprus summit following leaked Pentagon memo on Spain
stories.summary: A leaked internal Pentagon email proposing the suspension of Spain from NATO for refusing to support US-Israeli operations in Iran triggered a major transatlantic row at the Cyprus informal summit. EU leaders including those from Germany, France, and the Netherlands defended Spain; NATO stated its founding treaty has no mechanism for suspension. Leaders simultaneously debated strengthening EU Article 42.7 mutual defence obligations. These discussions formed the backdrop to Orpo's Cyprus attendance.

stories.headline: Stubb's Jordan and Egypt visit highlights Middle East instability, Ukraine war, and Finnish business delegation
stories.summary: President Stubb made an official two-day visit to Jordan (meeting King Abdullah II) followed by a two-day visit to Egypt (meeting President al-Sisi, PM Madbouly, and Al-Azhar grand imam), with discussions centring on the Iran-Israel conflict, Gaza, the Hormuz Strait, Ukraine, and transatlantic trade. A Finnish business delegation accompanied the president. Egyptian media gave the visit prominent coverage.

stories.headline: Stubb's 'shouting' communication style with Trump draws international 'Trump whisperer' label
stories.summary: During a visit to Canada, President Stubb revealed that he communicates with US President Trump partly by shouting, and rejected the 'Trump whisperer' label given to him in international media. Finnish commentators and a professor analysed what the communication style reveals about the Stubb-Trump relationship. Stubb emphasised that he and Trump have been friends for a long time and that not agreeing on everything is understood between them.

stories.summary: The Presidential Office announced President Stubb will make an official state visit to the Czech Republic on May 4-5, meeting President Petr Pavel and PM Andrej Babiš. The agenda includes bilateral relations, economic cooperation, European security, and Russia's war in Ukraine. Stubb will also participate in a conference on Europe's future and is accompanied by Social Affairs Minister Sanni Grahn-Laasonen and a business delegation.

stories.headline: Finland and Ukraine planning joint drone production on Finnish soil; Häkkänen confirms early-stage project
stories.summary: Defence Minister Häkkänen confirmed in parliament that Finland and Ukraine are in early-stage planning for joint production of unmanned systems on Finnish territory, in Finnish-Ukrainian joint ventures. Technical implementation details have not yet been defined. Häkkänen also confirmed the kehysriihi allocated additional funds across land, sea, and air defence procurement. Separately, Russia issued a warning that Finland would 'be a target.'

stories.headline: Häkkänen presses parliament to pass nuclear energy law enabling NATO nuclear hosting
stories.summary: Defence Minister Häkkänen urged parliament to pass amendments to Finland's nuclear energy law without procedural delay by the opposition, arguing the changed security environment and NATO membership make the changes legally necessary. The proposed amendment would allow Finland to host NATO nuclear assets, altering the basis of Finland's longstanding nuclear weapons policy.

stories.headline: OP Pohjola sets automatic security limits on all personal bank accounts to counter fraud wave
stories.summary: Finland's largest bank OP Pohjola announced it would automatically set daily and per-transaction security limits on all personal customer accounts during 2026, responding to a sharp rise in online banking fraud and phishing. The bank noted only around 20% of accounts currently have limits set. Customers can adjust the limits themselves through online banking.

stories.headline: Phishing and online fraud surge in Finland; Suomi.fi impersonation wave and new doorstep bank card theft tactic
stories.summary: Finnish authorities and telecoms industry body warned of a sharp rise in phishing attacks impersonating Suomi.fi, Kela, banks, and police services. Separately, Pohjanmaa police reported a new doorstep fraud tactic in which two suspects visited an elderly man's home, claiming to teach him a 'new way' to use his bank card, then stole card data and approximately €30,000. Banks including Nordea and Danske added new app-based limits in response to the fraud wave.

stories.headline: Parties begin nominating 2027 parliamentary election candidates across districts
stories.summary: Multiple Finnish parties including Kokoomus, SDP, Finns Party, Centre Party, Greens, Left Alliance, and Christian Democrats nominated their first candidates for the spring 2027 parliamentary elections across various electoral districts. The nominations mark the formal start of campaign season with roughly one year to go, set against a backdrop of declining governing-party poll support.

stories.headline: Bank of Finland developing offline payment system; Olli Rehn returns from cautious IMF/World Bank meetings
stories.summary: The Bank of Finland, together with other financial market authorities, is designing a system that would allow card payments to continue during internet or connectivity outages, with the Bank of Finland's Välimäki expressing hope it could be ready within a year. Separately, Bank of Finland Governor Olli Rehn published a blog post after the Washington IMF/World Bank spring meetings describing the global economic mood as serious but not hopeless, with uncertainty from multiple overlapping crises.
